📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that is there something going on today? A lot of talk about committing crimes and the like, I just can't quite put my finger on why… Ah well, couldn't be crucial or interesting. What is interesting, however, is Keepsake County, a "midwestern stealth game" that has launched on this inauspicious day about stealing stuff from "hideous farmhouses in the middle of nowhere.".

With the sarcastic intro out the way, I will address the elephant in the room: Vovly's Adventure: Reslimed is out today too. Fine, fine, yes I know GTA 6 is the game everyone's talking about, but Forward Instinct, the devs behind Keepsake County, seem well aware of that in their launch day post for the game: "Folks, thanks for your incredible patience. Keepsake County is finally OUT! And yes, it is deeply ironic that it wound up being today, of all days, that we got the green light to finally release, but here we are.".

Keepsake Country was supposed to release earlier this month, but seemingly got caught up in the backlog Valve are faced with that's undoubtedly been caused by genAI games. In any case, the burgle-em-up does look quite delightful. I'm not sure if I can quite put my finger on exactly why I get this feeling, but it calls to mind a more complex version of the kind of game you'd find on Cartoon Network's website back in the day (which is a high point of praise, I'd like to be clear).

In a recent development, each house in Keepsake Country is procedurally generated, meaning you never quite know what to expect when you enter. There's lockpicking, resident tie upping, and of course stealing to be done, but it doesn't just stop at the house. Parking your car, for instance, is an vital thing to consider; do you want it hidden so you're less likely to be discovered, or right at the front door so you can make a speedy escape? Not to mention you have to deal with the fuzz showing up at some point if you aren't quick enough!

Recent findings suggest that gear and the like can be improved between runs, meaning you can lockpick faster or delay the cops, it all seems quite systemically thoughtful. Very much some immersive sim vibes from this one, just on a much smaller scale. And most certainly worth considering picking up on a release day like today! If you're interested in doing so, you can pick it up on Steam right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upgrade [Tue 24th Nov 2026, 2:27pm]: Our sister site Push Square has also now published a guide for this Easter Egg:.

Original Story: One of the coolest things about GTA 6 since release has been watching players discover all kinds of Easter Eggs, such as the Mario-inspired hats that were shared by our sister site Nintendo Life yesterday.

We reckon this is the best one so far though - a secret portal that takes you into a nightclub from the original 2002 version of Vice City for the PS2 (which technically means it takes you back to its 1986-inspired setting).

The process of getting here is long-winded, and detailed in full in the video from Dan Allen Gaming up above. In a nutshell, you have to go to the Badger R&D Radio Tower in Key Lento and use the power switch and press a button to make the Malibu logo appear on the TV. From there, visit 12 LPL substations around the map without fast-travelling, and press the correct buttons in the specific order (from the video) when you reach them. You'll then get a text, at which point you head to Reactor 2 at the LPL Turtle Head Power Station between 7pm and 6am to find the portal.

It seems someone called Memelo was the first to discover this trick:.

According to recent reports, another really cool part of this Easter Egg is that when you combine all the substations together, the wording on the outside of them adds up to "Life is Passing Me By", which references a classic cheat code from the original Vice City. You actually have to use the buttons to enter this cheat code and make the portal appear.

As mentioned, you get two free items for your trouble as well, which are Tommy Vercetti's classic shirt and bike from the 2002 game. These appear as soon as you're thrown out of the portal and back into the so-called real world!

Finally, we'll also highlight that although pretty much all the footage we've seen of this Easter Egg has been exclusive to the Jason character, it does appear to work with Lucia as well. That noted, we've also come across many players who claim the portal isn't showing up for them, so we're not sure what's causing it to fail in those situations.

Anyway, crazy stuff right?! Who knows what other insane Easter Eggs might be discovered over the coming days and weeks - some people have mentioned they're seeing a "flashback" pop-up after completing the Vice City one, with a suggestion there may be another four flashback sequences yet to be found. Let's hope so!

Have you tried this? Did you get Tommy Vercetti's items? Let us know down in the comments sectiobn below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Industry observers note that gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good.".

Sources indicate that but like so many other ambitious latest studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain.".

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation.".

According to recent reports, "We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.".

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It says the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, said to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture announced last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

According to recent reports, these latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" revealed by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

In a recent development, since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Marvel Cinematic Universe is always expanding, and fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order are counting down the days until Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in December. Anticipation is high for the upcoming Marvel movie, especially because Doomsday's cast list includes entire teams of superheroes. That includes Channing Tatum's Gambit, who is clarifying comments about toning down his character's accent.

In a recent development, what we know about Avengers: Doomsday is limited, but Tatum finally gets the chance to join the X-Men in the blockbuster. Gambit's accent was fodder for jokes in Deadpool & Wolverine, with the other characters not being able to understand him. Although in an interview from The Associated Press' Instagram, he weighed in on chatter he'd be toning it down for the next Marvel blockbuster. In his words:.

I think I've been quoted in the press about toning down the accent. That is not exactly what I'm doing. I'm just speaking less Cajun French.

Recent findings suggest that honestly, this tracks. Tatum's Doomsday Dunkin' Ad featured him with Gambit's signature accent, and it was easy enough to understand the mutant as he spoke to H.E.R.B.I.E. about the coffee tech giant's seasonal treats. He's still going to be using the Cajun dialect, but won't be going so far as to use Cajun French throughout the course of the Avengers movie's runtime.

It has been revealed that later in the same interview, the Magic Mike icon went on to speak about the difference between the Cajun accent and Cajun French. In the 46 year-old actor's words:.

Recent findings suggest that it's hard to explain, but basically Cajun French is French that almost French people can't even understand. So I'm speaking less of that, but the Cajun accent's still there.

There you have it. Fans shouldn't expect Tatum to sound THAT much different than he did in Deadpool & Wolverine (which is streaming with a Disney+ subscription). He'll be using the same dialect, but won't be veering into French at all throughout the blockbuster. As such, the other heroes he interacts with will presumably be able to understand him.

It has been revealed that the final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday highlighted a bit more of Tatum's Gambit in battle, and his kinetic abilities look like they're going to be awesome in the movie's action sequences. We've seen him going to blows with Simu Liu's Shang-Chi, but it looks like he'll eventually work alongside The Avengers against Doctor Doom and his army of Sentinels.

Fans have been waiting a long time to see the card-throwing mutant take center stage, especially since Tatum was attached to a Gambit movie for years that sat in development hell. He's finally in the role, albeit under different circumstances.

The Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings sequel finally has some momentum behind it, as writer Dave Callaham reveals he's currently working on the follow-up.

The original movie, co-written by Callaham and director Destin Daniel Cretton, is a highlight of Marvel Phase 4 and was released back in 2021, but the sequel has been a long time coming.

It has been revealed that "I think I'm allowed to say, just to speak to a thing you said earlier, that I am working on a Shang-Chi sequel," Callaham shared on the Escape Hatch podcast. "So, hopefully – it's early stages, but we're getting some real movement, which is news. And so I'm really, really happy about that.".

Shang-Chi will next be seen in this December's Avengers: Doomsday, and, while the plot is still shrouded in mystery, the trailers so far have seen Shang-Chi in action against the threat of Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

According to recent reports, "When you really look at what happened to the industry, at least from my perspective, it was just like everything went to shit after that," Cretton has said previously of a Shang-Chi sequel. "I feel like if Marvel was where it was before, we would have had maybe two sequels already. Who knows?".

Sources indicate that as for where Shang-Chi has been all this time, star Simu Liu has ideas. "I actually think that he's much more likely to go back to Ta Lo," he has shared. "Just because he experiences for such a short period of time before stuff starts to go haywire. But it's really that peace of just remembering what it was like to drive through that for the first time, the experience of the animals but also to reconnect with his aunt and his family, I imagine that's probably really powerful for him.".

It has been revealed that avengers: Doomsday arrives this December 18. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV demonstrates.

Lead your band against hordes of enemies, auto-attacking with each character’s distinct Arts and weapons. Pairs of characters can also Interlink to form a mighty Ouroboros capable of taking down the most threatening enemies with powerful Arts.

Recent findings suggest that you can also test your strength against waves of enemies in the fresh Heroes’ Vault mode. Here, with each enemy you defeat, you’ll power up a gauge you can use to enhance your abilities and gain additional allies. GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.
  • The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn.
  • Sources indicate that as word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

Sources indicate that as word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

Recent findings suggest that and that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game debuted in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Sources indicate that either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the upcoming game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Upcoming Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

In a recent development, eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery.
  • It has been revealed that still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well.
  • Recent findings suggest that but nah, shotgun go boom boom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

It has been revealed that still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

Recent findings suggest that but nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing owners of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

In a recent development, it's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of Newly introduced Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

In a recent development, again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

According to recent reports, more impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

Sources indicate that "Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the latest edition.

Since it introduced on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

It has been revealed that another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard said WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most latest players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among fresh and returning players.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability enhancement.
  • According to recent reports, it's not all bad news, though.
  • One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability enhancement. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending latest orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

According to recent reports, it's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build new ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

According to recent reports, "We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

It's been 10 years since Quantum Break made its debut as an Xbox console exclusive in 2016, and Xbox fans have often considered it somewhat of an underated cult classic from the developer behind the likes of Control and Alan Wake.

Recent findings suggest that so, could we get a sequel?! Remedy Entertainment's X account has been talking about this over the last 24 hours, highlighting that the team love how much passion fans still have for the IP, but that the decision is in Xbox's hands.

In other words, it's down to Asha Sharma and her group at Xbox HQ.

Now, to be honest, we don't reckon it's a likely bet. The original Quantum Break was a really cool exclusive for Xbox to have 10 years ago, but it seems like the fresh Xbox CEO is more interested in focusing on big franchises like Gears, Halo, Fallout and The Elder Scrolls rather than dipping back into something from a difficult period in Xbox's history.

Recent findings suggest that that's not to say it couldn't happen though, and in some ways you'd think it'd be an easy win for Xbox to cater to nostalgia and remind everyone how much they enjoyed the original Quantum Break. Remedy has made sequels to Alan Wake and Control in recent times as well, so they'd surely be up for revisiting QB if given the opportunity.

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

Recent findings suggest that but Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

It has been revealed that in the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game rolled out, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Industry observers note that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game rolled out, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This upcoming leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Industry observers note that various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek notes the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

Industry observers note that cyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, yes, that's right – it could've been even bigger.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 might just be one of the biggest games of all time, with a map so vast it rivals the combined maps of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 – but, believe it or not, Rockstar cut some features from the latest Grand Theft Auto.

In a recent development, yes, that's right – it could've been even bigger. It's difficult to fathom, but Rockstar leads Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell reveal some of what was cut in a fresh interview with PCGames. The outlet first asks them about a tennis minigame, which exists in GTA 5. The two admit that developers initially planned to include tennis, but they weren't happy with how it was turning out, so they eventually axed it from the game.

Others, like minigolf, notably did make it in – but I suppose Rockstar was content with their implementation. Tennis isn't the only feature the studio scrapped, either. Jason and Lucia could've, uh, crawled, and they could've crafted items… survival sandbox game-style. The protagonists might also have been able to fully decorate and furnish their home, much like in The Sims 4 (and I'm especially distraught that decorating was cut).

Rockstar didn't think such features would make sense in Grand Theft Auto 6, both story-wise and in terms of gameplay – hence their removal. Nelson and Mitchell also point to more immersive elements that devs opted to remove, like movie theater visits, because they ultimately decided they weren't interactive enough. Again, I'm disappointed to learn these didn't make the final launch, but Rockstar probably made the right call.

After all, the GTA 6 they did release is smashing records as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and already standing as "the biggest launch in PlayStation history" (with Sony reporting "more than 39 million unique players" playing on just the PS5). It's clear the game is doing well – and that's an understatement – without the features, and potentially feels more fluid as is. I'll always be mad about the decorating, though.

  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet stated mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • Sources indicate that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet stated mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

Sources indicate that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

It has been revealed that ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

It has been revealed that outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft claims the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active consumers over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft unveiled in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Recent findings suggest that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

  • "Although both target 30fps and maintain it during typical gameplay, heavy vehicle traversal and intense airport crowd sequences cause frame-rates to drop into the mid to upper 20s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The good folks over at Digital Foundry are still busy analysing all things to do with GTA 6's launch last week, and their latest comparison takes a look at all four console versions alongside each other - Series X, S, PS5 and PS5 Pro.

It has been revealed that they also go on to rank the versions in order, and perhaps surprisingly, Xbox Series X comes out on top versus the standard PS5. Two reasons are given for this, which are that the Xbox version supports 120Hz VRR to smooth out the dips in frame rate, and that the PS5 sometimes "suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X".

"Although both target 30fps and maintain it during typical gameplay, heavy vehicle traversal and intense airport crowd sequences cause frame-rates to drop into the mid to upper 20s. PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off.".

Visually, there are mentioned to be no real differences between the Xbox Series X and PS5 versions, although the Series X version does have "slightly more pronounced heat haze effects in one opening shot".

All of this is obviously beaten by the PS5 Pro though, which is noted to "deliver the definitive console GTA 6 experience by leveraging its larger GPU, accelerated machine learning hardware and enhanced ray tracing features".

Sources indicate that "Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X - which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability. The Xbox Series S sits at the bottom due to visual trade-offs, unstable frame-rates and audio glitches.".

It's fair to say we never expected the Xbox Series X version to fare better than the PS5 version in this case, especially considering all the "plays best on PS5" marketing that surrounded GTA 6 prior to release.

It has been revealed that of course, Digital Foundry seeks out the most minute of details when it comes to technical analysis, and the differences between the Xbox Series X and standard PS5 versions aren't going to be major enough to suggest one version is far better than another. It's just interesting that they've ended up ranking the Series X higher in this instance.

Industry observers note that let us hear your thoughts in the comments, but please do keep it respectful! We enjoy the PS5 as well, and know plenty of people who are loving the game on that system. All the same, this is a fascinating analysis and a bonus for Xbox.

Shortly it debuted back in 2009, Ryan Murphy's campy musical comedy Glee became a sensation. The show has also been associated with a number of tragedies, with three main cast members having died, starting with Cory Monteith's death back in 2013. There's been chatter online about the "Glee curse" and now Tina actress Jenna Ushkowitz has issued a heartfelt response about that discourse.

Monteith's death broke the heart of fans and his coworkers alike, with the cast swiftly putting together a tribute episode in the midst of their grief. Since then there's been more tragedies with this talented ensemble, such as Naya Rivera's death in 2020. While appearing on the podcast We Need To Talk with Paul C. Brunson, Ushkowitz shared her emotional reaction to folks insensitively talking about the Glee curse.

My response to the Glee curse, as it’s always been, is we are human. And to hear that people see this as a collective curse that’s like, ‘Who’s next?’ is so unkind. And it shows the way in which we are able to just sit behind our computers and type off whatever we think we’re feeling in that moment without really connecting to what’s behind it and who’s on the other side.

Real people died, not characters, which has been a source for quite a bit of pain by the rest of the cast. Those feelings remain to this day, case in point being Harry Shum Jr. honoring Naya Rivera this season on Dancing with the Stars.

In addition to the death of Rivera and Monteith, Puck actor Mark Salling committed suicide back in 2018 before going to prison for possession of child sexual abuse imagery. What's more, an entire docuseries called The Price of Glee was released in 2023 examining the "curse." In the same podcast, Jenna Ushkowitz spoke more about the pain and grief that the cast has dealt with, offering:.

Sources indicate that we lost friends. People grieve those people. This is not something that’s, like, ‘Who’s next? This is a game.’ It’s not.

Sources indicate that the internet can be a cruel place, and the discourse about the Glee curse has clearly been painful for the cast. The tragic loss of their coworkers is hard enough, but the light-hearted chatter about these deaths has clearly created more pain for the members of the William McKinley High School Glee Club. Hopefully Ushkowitz's comments will circulate online, and help to quiet that type of talk.

According to recent reports, glee is streaming in its entirety over on Hulu, while fans patiently wait for news about Ryan Murphy's potential reboot. Our thoughts continue to be with the cast as they process their grief.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

Industry observers note that he gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

In a recent development, moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

Recent findings suggest that it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Sources indicate that best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm at the moment ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

According to recent reports, the Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

  • Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place".
  • "We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up upcoming possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up upcoming possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.

Sources indicate that you'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec mentioned. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

In a recent development, that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the firm affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38.

In a recent development, this is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

Another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

In a recent development, this Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.

Sources indicate that team Cherry, the outfit behind Hollow Knight and Silksong, has revealed Cherry Time, an upcoming livestream that'll contain details on Sea of Sorrow. This has fans incredibly excited, and fellow devs wary of when Sea of Sorrows may come out.

Aeternum Game Studios has had enough, though. "A little over a year ago, just as we were about to launch our game, you announced Silksong," the studio writes in an open letter to Team Cherry.

Recent findings suggest that "This time we're staying put," Aeternum states. "Not to go against you, but because a lot of people have been waiting for the Queen of Light for a long time, and we don't want to make them wait any longer.".

It has been revealed that that's true. Lucis is the third installment in the Aeterna series, after 2021's Aeterna Noctis and 2023's Summum Aeterna. There's a small but dedicated community who've been anticipating this latest chapter for a while.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Sources indicate that kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

Recent findings suggest that "We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

Spoilers for Season 3, Episode 7 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power are ahead! You can stream the entire third season with an Amazon Prime subscription now.

Sauron is one of the most legendary villains, and in Season 3 of The Rings of Power, we’ve really gotten to see him ascend to that level as he crafts the One Ring. In the seventh episode of the season airing on the 2026 TV schedule, he finally forged the terrifying piece of jewelry that causes a whole lot of problems in Middle-earth. While it was an epic moment to watch on TV, it turns out the story behind filming it is hilarious.

According to recent reports, knowing how much Charlie Vickers cares about Sauron and telling this story, I knew forging the One Ring would be a big moment for him behind the scenes. It’s also just objectively a huge moment in the season both from a lore perspective and a logistics perspective, seeing as the sequence from when he starts to forge the ring to the moment he puts it on is well over ten minutes long. When I asked Vickers about filming this, he told me why it was so exciting and rewarding to do:.

Industry observers note that it was amazing. It was twofold because like three seasons and getting to the point, like the seminal moment, was – that felt like a huge deal. But also getting to the end of that sequence, right? Because it's a long sequence when you watch it. It was a long sequence to film.

I can only imagine how long it took. Plus, it must have been exhausting, considering he was hammering the ring for quite some time. To that point, Vickers told me that while Sauron’s reward was the ring, his reward as an actor was simply getting to the end of the scene, as he said:.

It has been revealed that as Charlie, I also had a reward. My reward at the end of it was I get to hold the ring and lift up the ring, and finally say the ring poem. Because before that, it was a lot of hammering and a lot of broken hammers and blistering.

It has been revealed that alright, here’s where things get funny. As the Sauron actor was telling me this story, he went on a small tangent about the gloves he was wearing. It turns out he busted through one of them while filming all of this. However, if you want to know why, he hilariously can’t give you that answer:.

And there was one bit where, you know, when I'm like smashing the thing, oh, and the lava is raining down on me, and I have to go, ‘Ah! My hand's really hot,’ and I take off my gloves. I smashed my hand through the end of the glove. Like I just busted the glove open because, um, I don't know why that happens, but it was exhausting. So it was incredible.

I’d like to point out, and you can see this in the video above, that when Charlie Vickers said he didn’t know why he busted his glove open, Jamie Campbell Bower, who plays Celeborn and was sitting right next to him, burst out laughing. It really was hilarious, too. That’s because here we have arguably one of the most intense and anticipated moments in Rings of Power history, and the star of it – the man who plays Sauron – recalling said story in a very casual, chill and funny way.

Plus, the plot twist at the end of him breaking the glove and having no idea how he did it really was the nail in the coffin that got both me and the Celeborn actor giggling during the interview.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Anyway, silliness aside, this sequence is epic in Rings of Power. Vickers is so commanding as Sauron, and watching him forge the One Ring was surreal in a lot of ways. We’ve seen the iconic ring in The Lord of the Rings movies, and the last three seasons of Rings of Power have been building to it. So, to finally watch Sauron bring it into existence was incredible. And honestly, the funny story behind it makes it even better.

Now, considering we know Rings of Power Season 4 is happening, here’s hoping we get more legendary moments like this one and more silly stories behind them.

Any staff not intending to use the technology must explain why it's not a suitable fit.

Anonymous members of staff have spoken out to claim that if neither of the above are adhered to, projects will not be given the green light to proceed. One source states that while Ubisoft is not outright mandating the use of generative AI, the company is nevertheless "all-in" on the technology:.

Sources indicate that "We were told that using AI will increase the speed at which pitches can be made by 'small lean agile teams,' [meaning] prototypes could be built faster. We were told that as the goal was to move fast, iterate and discard projects to sift out the good stuff. AI was essential in maintaining a rapid pace. If you planned on not using it, you would have to have a reason.".

It's also been claimed that Ubisoft now believes generative AI to be "unavoidable", and is under the impression that most gamers simply don't care about its inclusion, with only a vocal minority opposing it.

It has been revealed that "Ubisoft is in a top-down nightmare of AI psychosis. Yves [Guillemot] has hitched his wagon to the tech, demanding the rest of the company follow on.".

Another source described the mood at Ubisoft as "abysmal", citing aggressive cost-cutting and a fresh mandate to work from the office full time.

It has been revealed that "Ubisoft still isn't replacing most people leaving the organization, leaving some teams stretched unbearably thin. Going-away parties [are] happening every couple [of] weeks it feels. The headless-chicken-core approach to generative AI is just the cherry on top, and Motherbrain is the smaller cherry on top of the cherry.".

As a reminder, 'Motherbrain' is the internal name devised for Ubisoft's AI initiative.

All this comes as Ubisoft continues to close studios and shed its staff. It most recently laid off 166 employees from Ubisoft Montréal and Québec while also shutting down RedLynx, the studio behind the critically-acclaimed Trials series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Capcom has unveiled it'll be delisting its multiplayer dinosaur shooter Exoprimal in March 2027, and then turning the game's servers off in September.

The news comes from an "end of service announcement" published on the official Exoprimal website, where it is said: "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

As of today, 25th November 2026, the game's four Survival Passes have already been taken off the PS Store.

Then, on 30th March 2027, Exoprimal and all its DLC and any other content will be removed from all storefronts.

Finally, the "end of service" phase and complete shutdown of Exoprimal is scheduled for 29th September 2027.

"Exoprimal will no longer be playable after the end of service," Capcom confirms. While the game did receive a physical release on a disc, it requires an internet connection to servers in order to play. With those gone, Exoprimal will stop functioning no matter whether you own it physically or digitally.

Sources indicate that capcom has enjoyed an incredible PS5 generation with multiple critically-acclaimed releases, but Exoprimal is one of the few titles it put out that fell below the standards it set. That's not to say Exoprimal was bad, though — far from it.

Sources indicate that in our own Exoprimal PS5 review, we awarded it a 7/10 and called it a "white-knuckle fusion of Overwatch and Gears of War". However, competition in the multiplayer space is strong, and it appears the game didn't do enough to sustain a substantial enough playerbase for Capcom to justify keeping the servers turned on.

Now, in less than a year, Exoprimal will be delisted and rendered completely unplayable.

The game is still full price on the PS Store, but between now and March 2027 (when the delisting occurs), I do imagine Capcom will hand it some steep discounts so those still curious can try it for cheap.

Did you play Exoprimal and enjoy it? Let us know in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

Sources indicate that however, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we presently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Sources indicate that using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

It has been revealed that this does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

According to recent reports, we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have mentioned about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

After learning more, Tresp, 16, told his mother, Khristina, about the exchange; she was initially suspicious, but after speaking with the girl directly on Discord and reading reports of her disappearance, she took action, asking for a piece of mail or document with a full name on it, which the girl provided.

It has been revealed that with that, Khristina began digging into tax and property records to find relevant addresses, which she then used to find photos on real estate sites. She indicated the photos to the missing girl on Discord, who picked out the one where she was being held; with that information in hand, Khristina contacted the girl's mother on social media and spoke to her briefly on the telephone, and also received a call from the FBI asking if she could confirm that the girl was still alive.

According to recent reports, "I said: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her'," Khristina told the BBC. "And she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'.".

Industry observers note that the kidnapped girl contacted Khristina the following morning, after her alleged captor, 39-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel, had left the house. In a conversation monitored by the FBI, she said she'd met Harmel on social media, where he'd pretended to be disabled and offered to pay her to help him get from Utah to Oregon. When he picked her up, however, he threw her phone into a river, then drove her to Oregon.

The girl told Khristina that she was kept in his basement and forced to sleep against the wall in his bed, while he kept a knife under his pillow to prevent escape. He gave her a mobile phone that wasn't able to make calls but could connect to wifi, which is how she was able to play online and eventually reach out for help.

Recent findings suggest that while Harmel was out, law enforcement began monitoring his street and house; when the moment came, police had Khristina tell the victim that it was time to make her escape. She was able to leave the house safely and into the custody of state troopers, while Harmel was subsequently arrested and charged with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Remember when Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot remarked the company was making the world's first AAAA video game with its mediocre pirate RPG Skull and Bones?
  • As reported by Game File, a lawsuit was filed against Ubisoft in 2025 by a gamer (and lawyer) who alleged that the manufacturer had violated Kansas' consumer protection act with its marketing of Skull and Bones, partly pointing to Guillemot calling it a AAAA game when trying to justify its $70 price tag in an earnings call.
  • In a recent development, obviously, when it came down to it, more than a few players disagreed with this sentiment, with a Metacritic score of 59 and a user score of 3.3 essentially dubbing it mid at best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Remember when Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot remarked the company was making the world's first AAAA video game with its mediocre pirate RPG Skull and Bones? Well, that terminology landed Ubisoft in a bit of hot water – which it may have gotten itself out of for now, but potentially not forever.

As reported by Game File, a lawsuit was filed against Ubisoft in 2025 by a gamer (and lawyer) who alleged that the manufacturer had violated Kansas' consumer protection act with its marketing of Skull and Bones, partly pointing to Guillemot calling it a AAAA game when trying to justify its $70 price tag in an earnings call. In the same call, Guillemot had called it "a very big game" that was "vast and complete," and stated it would "deliver in the long run.".

In a recent development, obviously, when it came down to it, more than a few players disagreed with this sentiment, with a Metacritic score of 59 and a user score of 3.3 essentially dubbing it mid at best. Certainly not what anyone was hoping for after over 10 years of development. Needless to say, the game-loving lawyer wasn't impressed, and in the initial lawsuit, it was alleged: "The statements by the CEO were misleading and enticed consumers to enter into consumer transactions to their detriment.".

Ubisoft, however, didn't agree that Guillemot had been misleading, calling his comments "subjective statements" and "classic puffery" – defined in this context as exaggerated statements not intended to be taken literally as fact. As such, the tech giant's lawyers argued: "Plaintiff has not identified a single objective statement about the game's quality that is demonstrably untrue, let alone one that he saw or relied on in purchasing the game as is required under the KCPA [Kansas Consumer Protection Act].".

However, the lawsuit argued that because Guillemot's comments were made during an earnings call, they were directed at investors rather than customers, and therefore the CEO "knew or should have known his statements would be relied upon as credible and truthful." The matter went "beyond mere puffery," it was argued.

Game File points out, though, just how 'AAAA' Skull and Bones is wasn't actually the focus of the argument. Rather, the main point was an alleged digital ownership concern, with claims that fans had been misled into thinking they'd own the game rather than simply its license – a license that, in theory, he could lose access to.

However, a judge sided with Ubisoft back in August. Even so, the lawyer suggested that he'll re-file it in California – Ubisoft had previously argued it required the case to be transferred there – so it might not be over for good yet.

In a recent development, whether that AAAA game comment comes back to bite Ubisoft again is another matter, though. Regardless of whether the firm is legally in the clear for using it, one CD Projekt Red exec previously appeared to poke fun at it, and more generally it doesn't seem likely that folks are going to let Ubisoft forget about it.
